comments.author: Bojan Radojicic
comments.comment: The hard part is not generating the report, it is proving every number has lineage back to source rows. I’d trust this fastest when the app treats AI output as a draft layer only, with deterministic checks for balances, mappings, and variance thresholds before any commentary gets reviewed.

comments.author: Umair Ahmad
comments.comment:
One thing I see teams underweight: eval data becomes platform infrastructure once agents start taking actions, not just answering.

A small, versioned eval set tied to real failure modes can save more money than another round of model routing, because it tells you when routing, retrieval, or tools actually got better.

Where do you see teams hit the first reliability wall: retrieval quality, tool execution, or observability?

comments.author: Connor Stevens
comments.comment:
The useful part is not the 32 skills, it is whether each skill has a clear input contract, approval boundary, and audit trail.

For HR workflows, I’d rather see a smaller set of agents that reliably escalate edge cases than a huge skill library that quietly drafts policy-sensitive output without context.

comments.author: Rizwan Tufail
comments.comment:
A policy tells you what people intended. An inventory tells you what can actually happen.

The sharp distinction for agentic systems is capability vs reach:
- capability: what the model/toolchain can decide or generate
- reach: what APIs, data, credentials, and side effects it can touch

Most incidents come from reach being larger than anyone realized.

What is the minimum inventory field you would require before an agent is allowed into production?

comments.author: Quentin Gavila
comments.comment:
The missing category I’d add is replayable eval infrastructure: same inputs, same retrieved context, same tool responses, same judge version.

Without that, agent “quality” turns into vibes fast, because every regression can hide behind nondeterminism.

What are you using to make failures reproducible before you tune the agent? #AgenticAI

comments.author: Joel Van Veluwen
comments.comment: The hard part is not keeping an agent running for 30 hours, it is defining what it is allowed to wake you up for. I’d want every always-on agent to have a small “interrupt budget” - maybe 3 pings/day max unless severity crosses a threshold. How are you deciding which findings deserve a notification versus a daily digest?
